_readme: Queue written by the daily-reel-render task, drained by tools/apply_additions.py during tools/sync.bat. The task must NOT edit calendar.md or review-state.json directly - it queues here instead, and sync.bat folds these in AFTER pulling, on top of whatever the desk decided today. That is what stops the two files conflicting. Adds only: an existing calendar row (keyed on date + post title) is left exactly as the desk left it, and so is an existing review-state key - with one exception, the render flip (content: awaiting-render or rerender -> in-review, plus new revisions entries), which is what tells the desk a cut now exists. It can never write an approval; see the module docstring in tools/apply_additions.py.

revisions.changed: Initial cut of "It didn't affect the play": 16.3, 16.3.1, 16.3.2. Seven scenes, two-pair shape, 889 frames at 29.63s, 1080x1920, 30fps. Layout reproduces the 2026-09-08 dry measure exactly (main scenes 1192, details 554 and 740, tip 1062, closing 900, 0 problems, no collisions); check_dull passes at 0.23s against the 0.45s threshold; all three rule texts byte-identical to rules.json and all three _payload() quote pairs present in the PNGs. Built outside the sandbox, which would not mount: Chromium rasterised the SVGs in place of ImageMagick and Arial stood in for Liberation Sans, both metric-compatible substitutions validated on carousel-post-5, and the encode used a bundled ffmpeg with encode.py's arguments unchanged.
